Mac mini or Linux VPS for Claude Code and Codex?

Reviewed: 2026-11-08 · WodeMac

A Linux VPS is usually cheaper and is enough for backend, script and web projects if you are happy with SSH. Anything that needs macOS, such as Xcode, iOS and Mac apps or Safari testing, needs a real Mac, because Apple's license allows macOS only on Apple hardware. If you want a full desktop, a preinstalled setup or one dedicated computer per team member, a remote Mac mini is the simpler choice.

When a Linux server is enough

  • Your project is a web app, API, script or data pipeline whose builds and tests run on Linux.
  • You are comfortable with SSH and tmux and do not need a graphical desktop.
  • Budget comes first and you will install and maintain the agents and runtimes yourself.

When it has to be a Mac

  • Building, testing or signing iOS, iPadOS or macOS apps: Xcode and simulators run only on macOS.
  • Testing in Safari or WebKit.
  • Projects that depend on Mac desktop software or automation.
  • Teams that want each person to have a dedicated computer with a full desktop rather than a shared shell.

Apple's macOS Software License Agreement permits macOS only on Apple-branded hardware, so there is no legitimate macOS on a generic Linux or Windows cloud host.

FAQ

Can I install macOS on a cloud VPS to run Xcode?

No. Apple's license allows macOS only on Apple-branded hardware, so generic Linux or Windows cloud hosts cannot legitimately run it. For Xcode you need a real Mac.

Is Claude Code the same on Linux and macOS?

The core features are the same. Officially supported systems include macOS 13+, Ubuntu 20.04+ and Debian 10+. The difference comes from which toolchain your project needs.

What does a remote Mac mini cost?

WodeMac charges $169 monthly, $481.65 quarterly, $912.60 half-yearly or $1,723.80 yearly for the machine only; Claude or OpenAI usage is billed separately by those providers.
